subject.title: [Bug]: iOS app fails to connect over Tailscale CGNAT (100.x.x.x) — wss:// required but WebSocket upgrade silently dropped

question: Should iOS remote/Tailscale pairing keep the current secure-only policy with clearer Tailscale Serve/direct-CGNAT diagnostics, or should direct Tailnet CGNAT get a supported plaintext or TOFU path?
rationale: The remaining behavior sits on mobile TLS, fingerprint trust, setup-code bootstrap, and Gateway exposure policy; automation cannot safely decide whether to preserve fail-closed secure transport or create a new trusted-private-network exception.

options.title: Keep Secure-Only And Fix Diagnostics
options.body: Preserve `wss://` for non-LAN mobile routes, steer users to Tailscale Serve/MagicDNS or a pinned certificate, and make raw CGNAT/no-TLS failures actionable in onboarding and Settings.

options.title: Approve Direct Tailnet Exception
options.body: Allow an explicit, tested, and documented direct-CGNAT path such as trusted private-network plaintext or TOFU, with clear warnings and no public-host downgrade.

options.title: Defer To Broader Remote Pairing
options.body: Leave this issue open while the overlapping iOS onboarding and public `wss://` guidance items settle the supported remote pairing story.

recommendation.title: Keep Secure-Only And Fix Diagnostics
recommendation.body: Preserve `wss://` for non-LAN mobile routes, steer users to Tailscale Serve/MagicDNS or a pinned certificate, and make raw CGNAT/no-TLS failures actionable in onboarding and Settings.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged route-list work and adjacent security-doc ownership make steipete the strongest available owner for the mobile remote-pairing trust-boundary choice.
